title: Comparing GitHub Pricing 2026 Plans and Hidden Costs
summary: GitHub pricing structures dictate your monthly software development expenses based on team size and required security features.
body_markdown:
## GitHub pricing and plan features compared


GitHub pricing is per user: Free costs $0, Team costs $4 per user monthly, and Enterprise costs $21 per user monthly. Free includes 2,000 Actions minutes and 500MB of storage. Team includes 3,000 minutes and 2GB. Enterprise includes 50,000 minutes, 50GB and SSO. Copilot Enterprise costs $39 per user monthly.


GitHub’s pricing structure uses a per-seat model that scales with headcount regardless of how often each user touches the code. As of September 2026, the platform has four distinct tiers that gate security and automation resources behind per-user premiums.


### GitHub Free for individuals and small teams


$0 per month forever is the entry point for[GitHub Free](https://github.com/pricing) , meaning a startup can host unlimited public and private repositories without an upfront financial commitment.


While the price is accessible, it limits GitHub Actions to 2,000 minutes per month. 500MB is the cap for storage, which prevents the hosting of large binary assets, forcing teams to seek external solutions for their media files.


### GitHub Pro for advanced personal projects


Individual power users who require more than the basic automation limits but do not need organizational management tools are the target for GitHub Pro.


It increases the Actions allowance to 3,000 minutes, providing a 50% buffer over the free tier for developers running complex test suites.


Per-seat pricing turns every new hire into a recurring line item, often leading IT to restrict access to a small group while the rest of the company waits on a growing backlog.


Activepieces addresses this by metering by consumption rather than headcount; since credits track usage and unlimited flows ship on every plan, adding a team member costs nothing until they actually run an automation.


> Per-seat pricing turns every new hire into a recurring line item, often leading IT to restrict access to a small group while the rest of the company waits on a growing backlog.


Organizations like Alan and Funding Societies use this structure to scale production workflows without headcount-driven cost spikes, keeping credentials centrally managed instead of scattered across individual logins.


### GitHub Team for growing organizations


At $4 per user/month, GitHub Team introduces the first significant per-seat multiplier for growing companies, effectively turning infrastructure overhead into a variable expense that scales directly with headcount. Michaeleakins reports that this plan increases storage to 2GB, allowing teams to maintain larger build artifacts and Docker images directly within the platform. The most critical shift is the variable cost of compute for automation.


- Linux 2-core runners cost[$0.006 per minute](https://docs.github.com/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing) , so a simple script running hourly costs roughly $4.32 a month.
- Windows 2-core runners cost[$0.010 per minute](https://docs.github.com/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing) , meaning cross-platform testing is about 67% more expensive than standard Linux builds.
- macOS 12-core runners cost[$0.077 per minute](https://docs.github.com/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing) , so mobile developers pay a premium for Apple-specific build environments.
- Ubuntu 64-core runners cost[$0.162 per minute](https://docs.github.com/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing) , which means high-performance builds for massive monorepos can easily exceed the base subscription cost in a single afternoon.


The following table summarizes how these tiers compare across the core resource dimensions that dictate your monthly bill.


2026 Plan Price (per user) Actions Minutes Storage Support


Free $0 2,000 500MB Community


Team $4 3,000 2GB Standard (Business Hours)


Enterprise $21 50,000 50GB 24/7 Premium


*Prices and plan limits checked against[github.com](https://github.com/pricing) on September 29, 2026.*


**A 425% increase in base cost per employee occurs during the jump from $4 to $21.** This forces leadership to justify the added value of the premium tier against a much steeper financial commitment.


### GitHub Enterprise for scale and compliance


GitHub Enterprise costs $21 per user/month, a price point justified primarily by the inclusion of Single Sign-On (SSO) and advanced compliance auditing.


By providing 50,000 Actions minutes, it eliminates the risk of build-minute overages for most organizations, though the high per-seat cost means a company of 100 people pays $25,200 annually just for access.


This tier is the only option for companies that require audit logs and centralized identity management to meet SOC2 or ISO 27001 requirements.
